# `silk/bench/transport`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Carries the lines of the driven benchmark protocol between a benchmark task and a harness.

## When to use
Provide a [`StreamTransport`](#StreamTransport) to a `silk.bench.harness.Harness` so that a benchmark task can
drive your program. Implement [`Transport`](#Transport) yourself to drive a harness that standard input
and output cannot reach: one on another computer behind a socket, or one in a sandbox that
only shares files.

## Details
The driven protocol is a dialogue of lines, and this service is all of it that touches the
outside: [`Transport.receive`](#Transport.receive) takes the next line from the other side, and
[`Transport.send`](#Transport.send) gives it one. Neither side of the protocol knows what carries the lines.

The task sends one command a line, and the harness answers each with lines that end with
the line `done`:

```text
task     list
harness  BenchmarkParse/file=twitter
harness  BenchmarkWrite
harness  done
task     run BenchmarkParse/file=twitter 2000
harness  BenchmarkParse/file=twitter 2000 165412.50 ns/op
harness  done
task     quit
```

- `list` asks for the names of the benchmarks, one a line.
- `run <name> <iterations>` asks for one sample: the harness runs the body that many times
  and answers with one result line, as `silk.bench.lines` describes them. It may send
  configuration lines such as `check: 9f2c41aa` before the result line.
- `quit` ends the harness. The end of the input means the same.

A harness in another language reads and writes these lines on its standard input and
output. The task starts it with the environment variable `BENCH_DRIVE` set to `1`.

[`StreamTransport`](#StreamTransport) carries the lines over two descriptors: [`StreamTransport.standard`](#StreamTransport.impl.standard) is
standard input and output, which is what a harness uses, and [`StreamTransport.over`](#StreamTransport.impl.over) is any
pair, which is what the task uses for the pipes of a harness it started.

## Gotchas
[`StreamTransport`](#StreamTransport) works on Linux with GNU libc and on macOS. On another system, every
operation fails.

## Examples
```silk
import silk.bench.transport { Transport, TransportError }
import silk.collections.list { List }
import silk.core.effect { Effect }
import silk.core.option { Option }
import silk.mem.allocator { Allocator, OutOfMemoryError }
import silk.text.string { String }

// A transport that answers from memory, as a test of a harness would use.
struct Scripted {
  commands: List<String>,
  next: usize,
  answers: List<String>,
}

impl Transport for Scripted {
  effect fn receive(self: &mut Self) -> Option<String>
    ! TransportError | OutOfMemoryError
    ? &mut Transport | &mut Allocator {
    if self.next == self.commands.length() {
      return Option<String>.None
    }
    self.next = self.next + 1
    return Option<String>.Some {
      value: run String.copy(self.commands.asSlice()[self.next - 1].view()),
    }
  }

  effect fn send(self: &mut Self, line: string) -> ()
    ! TransportError | OutOfMemoryError
    ? &mut Transport | &mut Allocator {
    return run self.answers.append(run String.copy(line))
  }
}

// Echoes every command back until the input ends.
effect fn echo() -> ()
  ! TransportError | OutOfMemoryError
  ? &mut Transport | &mut Allocator {
  let mut more = true
  while more {
    match move run Transport.receive() {
      Option<String>.Some { value } => {
        run Transport.send(value.view())
      }
      Option<String>.None => {
        more = false
      }
    }
  }
}

effect fn check() -> i32 ! TransportError | OutOfMemoryError ? &mut Allocator {
  let mut scripted = Scripted {
    commands: List<String>.make(),
    next: 0,
    answers: List<String>.make(),
  }
  run scripted.commands.append(run String.copy("list"))
  run scripted.commands.append(run String.copy("quit"))
  run echo() |> Effect.provideMut<Transport>(&mut scripted)
  if scripted.answers.length() != 2 || scripted.answers.asSlice()[1].view() != "quit" {
    return 1
  }
  return 0
}

effect fn failed(error: TransportError | OutOfMemoryError) -> i32 {
  drop error
  return 2
}

pub fn main() -> i32 {
  let mut allocator = Allocator.systemAllocatorProvider()
  return run Effect.catchAll(check(), failed) |> Effect.provideMut<Allocator>(&mut allocator)
}
```

<a id="Transport"></a>

## `Transport`

```silk
pub service Transport
```

What carries the lines of the driven protocol to the other side and back.

<a id="Transport.receive"></a>

### Operation `receive`

```silk
effect fn receive() -> Option<String>
    ! TransportError | OutOfMemoryError
    ? &mut Transport | &mut Allocator
```

Returns the next line from the other side, without its line end, or nothing when the
other side has ended.

#### Errors
- `TransportError` if the line cannot be read.
- `OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` cannot supply the line.

<a id="Transport.send"></a>

### Operation `send`

```silk
effect fn send(line: string) -> ()
    ! TransportError | OutOfMemoryError
    ? &mut Transport | &mut Allocator
```

Gives `line`, which holds no line end, to the other side.

#### Errors
- `TransportError` if the line cannot be written.
- `OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` cannot supply working memory.

<a id="StreamTransport"></a>

## `StreamTransport`

```silk
pub struct StreamTransport
```

A transport over two descriptors: lines are read from one and written to the other.

### Details
Both descriptors may be blocking or nonblocking: an operation waits until the descriptor is
ready. The transport does not close them.
